TWO THINGS CHANGED FOR `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` BETWEEN 2026-08-06 AND 2026-08-09, AND NEITHER IS A NEW IDEA — the question, the four options and Anthony's lean were already recorded. This is evidence against them.

=== ✅ (1) THE STATED PREREQUISITE IS MET ===

That node closes with: "⚠️ THE PREREQUISITE THAT STILL BOUNDS ALL OF IT: dec:linked-repos-poc was RUN 2026-08-06 and found reflow2 declares NO `required` interface at all, so nothing pairs across any seam. The channel this node is about has no labelled boundary to run along."

MEASURED 2026-08-09 against the committed export: **14 Interfaces, of which 9 are `required` and 3 `published`** — ifc:ambient-agent, ifc:authenticating-gateway, ifc:exclusive-local-store, ifc:mcp-protocol, and the five dynograph-foundation APIs. PR #130 (2026-08-09) landed this; `paired` went 0→5 and `seam_report` ran for the first time. **THE SEAM NOW HAS A LABELLED BOUNDARY. The blocker named in that node no longer holds.**

⭐⭐ AND ONE OF THOSE NINE ANSWERS THE OTHER HALF OF THE QUESTION. The 2026-08-06 node said what was missing was TRANSPORT and ENFORCEMENT, and that enforcement was unfixable: "nothing stops a writer doing more than filing, because reflow2 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION and cannot acquire one without becoming a different product." **`ifc:authenticating-gateway` is now a DECLARED REQUIRED INTERFACE** — "an authenticating gateway in front; reflow2 has no authentication." The hole did not close, but it stopped being an unstated hole and became a stated DEPENDENCY, which is a different thing: the design now says somebody else must provide this, and names the shape. **flo2 is a candidate provider of exactly that interface**, which makes the two projects' relationship reciprocal rather than one-directional.

=== 🔁 (2) THE MANUAL WORKAROUND RECURRED, AND ITS COST IS NOW STATED BY ITS AUTHOR ===

The 2026-08-06 node recorded the first occurrence: flo2 hit a wall it could not climb from inside itself, a human wrote a markdown proposal in the flo2 repo, a human read it, an agent re-typed it as reflow2 nodes, and NOTHING IN EITHER GRAPH KNEW.

IT HAPPENED AGAIN, 2026-08-09, in Anthony's words: "Earlier, I was working a bit on flo2 (projectB) and it will require some changes be made to reflow (projectA) to make it scalable to multiple users/multiple projects simultaneously. What I did earlier was ask the agent in flo2 what those changes will be. I then created a .md file and had the agent doing reflow2 session read that markdown file. **THAT IS HUGELY INEFFICIENT.**"

⭐ WHY A SECOND OCCURRENCE IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT: a workaround performed ONCE is an anecdote; a workaround performed TWICE, by the design's own author, on the design's own flagship dependency, is a measurement of what the absent feature costs. And the second time he named the cost himself rather than being asked.

=== THE OWNERSHIP SHAPE, STATED PLAINLY FOR THE FIRST TIME ===

Anthony, 2026-08-09: projectA (reflow2) and projectB (flo2) are both his responsibility; projectB is CO-DEVELOPED with his brother; projectB DEPENDS ON projectA; and **"my brother who is building the web app around reflow2 doesn't need access to projectA."**

That is not a new constraint — it is the same one the 2026-08-06 node built option (A) around — but it is now stated as a fact about the actual arrangement rather than as a hypothetical, and it independently re-confirms his lean: write-only-at-proposed keeps the brother out of reflow2 entirely while still letting flo2 levy what it needs.

⚠️ WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT DO: it does not choose an option. (A), (B), (C) and (D) all stand exactly as recorded, with (C) still refuted by the Google-service argument and (A) still carrying its honest counter — that reflow2 CANNOT ENFORCE write-only-at-proposed, because that is a property of whatever holds the mailbox. The blocker clearing makes the question ANSWERABLE; it does not answer it.
